chunks: I was with Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), and a man complained to him, saying, 'My children have been disobedient to me and my brothers have cut me off, and my (fellow Muslim) brothers have alienated themselves from me.' Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Truth has a dynasty (period of dominance), and falsehood has a dynasty. And in each one of them, the other is humiliated. And the least affliction that befalls a believer during the dynasty of falsehood is that his children are disobedient to him and his brothers cut him off, and his (fellow Muslim) brothers alienate themselves from him. And no believer experiences ease and comfort in the dynasty of falsehood except that he is tested in his body, wealth, or family, until Allah the Exalted purifies him of the luxury he had acquired in the dynasty of falsehood, so that his share may be reserved for him in the dynasty of truth. Therefore, be patient and rejoice.'

key_terms.جَفَانِي: They alienated themselves from me / cut ties
key_terms.عَقَنِي: My children were disobedient to me

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of familial alienation for believers during times of falsehood?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) contextualizes the believer's suffering within the cosmic struggle between the 'state of truth' and the 'state of falsehood,' framing social alienation and familial estrangement as minor trials in the latter. He further explains that any worldly ease enjoyed during the dominance of falsehood is inevitably tested through body, wealth, or family to purify the believer, thereby preserving their ultimate reward for the era of truth. This perspective encourages patience (sabr) and glad tidings (bashara), reinforcing the Shia eschatological hope that current hardships are temporary precursors to divine justice.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 31. It has been narrated that Abu al-Sabah reported:

I was with Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s) when a man complained to him saying, 'My son and my brothers have cut themselves off from me and my (fellow Muslim) brothers have (also) alienated themselves from me.' 'Truth (haqq) has a dynasty,' replied Abu 'Abd Allah (a.s), 'and so does falsehood (batil). And in each one of them, the other is disgraced. During the rule of falsehood, the least affliction that befalls a believer is that his sons and brothers break ties with him and his (fellow Muslim) brothers abandon him. And if a believer experiences a life of ease and comfort in the dynasty of falsehood, he will be afflicted in his physical body, wealth or family until Allah purifies him of the luxury that he had acquired in order that his share may thereby be reserved in the dynasty of truth. Therefore be patient and rejoice.”
